newsitem.title: USA: US Mid-Atlantic spot power flat after recent climb.
newsitem.headline: US Mid-Atlantic spot power flat after recent climb.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic region were mostly flat Wednesday versus Tuesday's level after recent gain on surging natural gas prices and unplanned outages of two nuclear plants.
"Prices were getting a bit high," said a Mid-Atlantic trader, adding buying interest eased today.

Tranmission limit in parts of the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool because of a damaged PECO Energy substation north of Philadelphia helped push prices higher Monday and Tuesday.
Restriction on the grid pressured some utilities to fire up more expensive oil or natgas generation to compensate for reduced amount of coal and nuclear power from the western part of PJM.
News of a fire at a power substation, operated by Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc, had little effect in the PJM market.

At least one PJM utility, Public Service Electric and Gas Co, aided ConEd by sending 600 megawatt (MW) of electricity to the New York Power Pool because the fire shut six high-voltage transmission lines that normal carry power from northern to southern New York.
At the New York City gate, natgas for swing delivery was quoted near $3.30 per million British thermal units.
The 1,090 megawatt MW Susquehanna 1 nuclear power unit, which was shut Monday to repair a steam drain pipe leak, was scheduled to resume service early next week.
A startup date for the 610 MW Oyster Creek nuclear power plant, idled since last Friday, remained unclear.
Firm, peak PJM electricity for Thursday was quoted at $24.75-$25.50 a megawatt hour (MWh), down from Tuesday's $26.00-$26.50 on mainly a lack of prescheduled activity.
November PJM electricity for firm, peak delivery was assessed at $23.75-$24.50, better offered than a range of $23.75-$24.25 late Tuesday.
December PJM power with similar delivery conditions was discussed between $28.30 and $29.00, a wider range than Tuesday's $28.50-$29.00.
January/February 1997 PJM deliveries were pegged at $32.15-$32.50, a tad lower than $32.25-$32.60 on Tuesday.
First-quarter 1997 PJM electricity held again at $29.60-$30.00.
